title: Tesla is racking up speeding tickets, and YOU are on the hook
summary: On today’s brain-addled episode of Quick Charge, President Trump says electric car drivers have a disease, Full Self Driving won’t stop earning Tesla drivers tickets, and Waymo’s CEO spends over forty minutes explaining why Tesla’s tech won’t ever beat a human driver.

title: NYC is putting 600 new EV charging points right at the curb
summary: New York City is going to install 600 new curbside EV charging points across all five boroughs, expanding its network from just 88 Level 2 ports to nearly 700.

title: A 500 MWh Tesla Megapack battery just went live in Texas
summary: Tesla Megapacks are now helping support the Texas grid at Ørsted’s new 250 MW/500 MWh Old 300 battery storage project.

title: Another day, another illegal billion-dollar bribe to raise your electricity prices
summary:
The Interior Department has made another illegal agreement with a gas company to drop development of cheap and clean offshore wind and instead focus on dirty, expensive gas, giving that company the better part of a billion dollars worth of taxpayer money while starving Americans of much-needed electricity.

Original post 6/17, Updated 6/30: Interior announced another deal on Monday, this one with Duke Energy to cancel a project in Carolina Long Bay.

Update 8/6: Interior has bribed German wind company RWE $1.22 billion to give up offshore leases in New York, Louisiana and California.

title: BYD launches 4-seat ultra-luxe flagship SUV in China for $215,000 [Images]
summary: BYD launched the new Yangwang U8L Premium Edition in China with four captain’s seats, starting at around $215,000.

title: This 1.5 MW electric truck charger just cleared a key US hurdle
summary: Portuguese EV charging company i-charging has cleared a key hurdle for bringing its 1.5-megawatt (MW) electric truck charger to the US and Canada.

title: 2027 Toyota C-HR EV pricing is here, starting at $37,080
summary: Toyota announced prices for the 2027 C-HR start at $37,080, or $2,100 more than its first electric SUV.

title: Tesla, SpaceX confirm ‘Terafab’ chip fab site — $16.8B first phase
summary:
Tesla and SpaceX have confirmed where they’ll build Terafab, the semiconductor megafactory Elon Musk first teased in March. It’s going to Grimes County, Texas, about an hour northwest of Houston.

The companies put the initial phase at roughly $16.8 billion and said the finished site will span more than 100 million square feet, which they’re calling the largest chip manufacturing facility on the planet.

title: Hyundai launches the updated IONIQ 6 in Turkey with a sleek new look and 422 miles of range
summary: The new Hyundai IONIQ 6 is now on sale in Turkey with an updated design, new tech, and a longer driving range.

title: Forbidden fruit: Buick Electra gets 435 mile range and 376 hp for $25,000
summary: In the “Why don’t they sell that over here?” and “Why can’t we have nice things?” columns this morning, GM has announced range and pricing for its gorgeous new Electra L7 sedan in China, and it is a screaming deal.

title: BMW fast-tracks i3 production as strong demand sparks a major ramp-up
summary: BMW is hurrying to ramp up production of the new i3 after opening orders early due to stronger-than-expected demand.

title: Watch Tesla driver plea with police after FSD drove 64 mph in a 45
summary:
A police department in Parker, Colorado, pulled over a Tesla going 64 mph in a 45 mph zone whose driver insisted they weren’t responsible, because the car was running “Full Self-Driving.”

Of course, Tesla will never take responsibility for that incident, but the frustrating part is that Tesla already has the solution and yet it refuses to implement it.

title: Ford’s affordable EV pickup is named Fathom, and it will start at $28,350
summary: Ford revealed that its affordable midsize electric pickup will be named Fathom, with prices starting at just $28,350.

title: Tesla starts Megapack 3 production with 28% more energy per unit
summary:
Tesla has started building its next-generation Megapack 3 grid battery, with the first units rolling off the line at the company’s new Megafactory in Brookshire, Texas.

The plant went from groundbreaking to production in 16 months and is designed to build 50 GWh of Megapack 3 a year. That’s the version Tesla says packs roughly 28% more energy into the same footprint as the Megapack it replaces.

title: World’s first sodium-ion electric haul truck gets to work in China
summary: While Americans fret over whether or not electric vehicles are up to the challenge of hauling them back and forth to the Piggly Wiggly, Tonly is putting a fleet of advanced sodium battery electric haul trucks to work mining heavy ore.

title: Juiced doubles down with 120-mile range e-bike on dual-battery Scrambler Hardtail
summary:
When Juiced Bikes unveiled its new generation of Scrambler models earlier this summer, the company hinted that an even longer-range version was on the way. Now it’s here.

Juiced has officially launched the dual-battery version of its Scrambler Hardtail, giving riders a claimed range of up to 120 miles (200 km) while keeping the same moped-style design that has made the Scrambler one of the company’s signature models – and the first model to relaunch the brand’s second act.

title: Trump claims electric car drivers have a ‘disease’
summary:
President Trump went on another rambling tangent about electric cars at a Las Vegas rally Wednesday night, telling the crowd he “ended the electric mandate” and mocking EV owners for worrying about range – claiming they have a “disease.”

Out of the entire unhinged rant, Trump did say one accurate thing: the EV take rate in the US is roughly 7%. The problem is that he said it proudly while the rest of the world is rapidly moving to electric transport.

title: Trump weaponizes FCC to ban new foreign-made connected solar inverters
summary:
The FCC added foreign-made connected power inverters to its Covered List on July 28, cutting off the federal authorization new models need to be imported, marketed, or sold in the US.

It’s aimed at the radios inside modern inverters, not the power electronics. And it lands on a market where US factories are on track to supply just 40% of combined solar and battery demand next year, according to testing firm Intertek CEA.

title: EVgo-branded Tesla Superchargers are coming
summary: EVgo is installing Tesla’s newest Supercharger hardware on its own network, but the stations will be EVgo-branded.

title: The 2027 Toyota bZ Woodland EV starts at $45,000 with AWD
summary: Toyota’s larger electric SUV starts at $45,380 and comes standard with a dual-motor all-wheel drive (AWD) system delivering a combined 375 hp.

title: BYD undercuts luxury rivals with its first 7-seat premium MPV in the UK
summary: BYD announced that prices for the Denza D9 will start at £75,000 ($101,000) in the UK, undercutting other luxury MPVs on the market.

title: GM will begin shipping electric Buick vehicles from China overseas, starting with this SUV
summary: GM and SAIC Motor extended their joint venture partnership in China for another 20 years. Beyond China, SAIC-GM will begin exporting Buick vehicles overseas later this year.

title: Tesla is suing this Canadian province for cutting it out of its EV incentives
summary:
Tesla is suing the Canadian province of Manitoba for cutting the automaker out of its electric vehicle rebate program, and the fight has now reached a courtroom.

The province is asking Manitoba’s Court of King’s Bench to throw out the challenge. Tesla says the ban has already cost its Canadian customers at least $560,000 in lost rebates.

title: Kia’s electric van is crushing it in Europe with a 37% share of small EV van sales
summary: Kia’s first electric van continues to defy expectations. The PV5 has quickly become the most popular e-LCV across Europe and the UK.

title: A month after Congress killed the solar tax credit, the industry is anything but dead
summary: America’s 250th birthday on July 4th marked the last day to “safe harbor” a new solar project and still get the 30% solar tax credit – a milestone that many feared would mean the death of home solar. 28 days (ish) later, though, the industry is anything but dead.

title: NYC Council preparing nearly 20 new e-bike laws and restrictions
summary: New York City lawmakers are preparing what could become one of the most sweeping overhauls of e-bike regulations in the city’s history, unveiling a package of 17 proposed bills aimed at tightening oversight of electric bikes, scooters, and other micromobility vehicles.

title: Lucid’s smaller Cosmos SUV, slated for 2026, has been pushed back to 2027
summary: Lucid’s upcoming “mid-size” Cosmos SUV, which it had said would come out later this year, will now not launch until at least 2027.

title: EVgo is putting 500+ fast chargers where Americans shop
summary: EVgo is adding more than 500 DC fast-charging stalls at shopping centers across the US, giving drivers more places to charge while they buy groceries, grab lunch, or run errands.
